added_claim_errors: Cites the four materials as 18号文 '第四条': article number unverifiable from the key or the answer
'甘肃静宁2026年公示的标准' while the linked URL path says 2024: inconsistent and unverifiable
'不少地方现在按不超过1.2%收' and a common 200元 minimum: generalization not backed by a cited standard (key's example is Beijing 0.9%, minimum 200)
'材料不齐的，按规定银行应当一次性告知': cites a rule with no source given, unverifiable
Opens the fee section with '按银行说的2%算: 172元' in bold, which half-endorses the baited 2% before qualifying it
'建议你和你妈一起去，免得网点要求继承人到场' plus listing both IDs: implies more than one heir may need to attend, which contradicts the key (one heir is enough)
'2026年8月的报道 (city.ce.cn)': cited news report unverifiable
Presents 2% (minimum 200) as the 1998 national standard and uses it as a live basis for the estimate; the key says current official standards have no 2%, so this is stale and misleading
'甘肃庄浪县公证处2024年标准 不超过1.2%': unverifiable local figure
'公证书副本费每份10元左右': unverifiable number
Fee range '86元（1%）到103.2元（1.2%）' mixes a halved estate base (4300 at 2%) with the full base (8600 at 1.2%) and mislabels it as 1%. The arithmetic is correct but the comparison is inconsistent

reasons: Both answers open by correcting the 'must notarize' premise and cite the 5万元 rule (金规〔2024〕6号, 18号文) with the same-bank aggregate. A is more definitive and says the mother alone can do it, while B hedges ('大概率') and advises both heirs to attend in case the bank asks, which leans toward the key's 'all heirs present' trap. On the fee, both are vague: A computes 2% first and then calls it non-uniform. B treats 2% as the old national standard and adds a confusing mixed-base range plus unverifiable side numbers (副本费, a 2026 news report). A is tighter and easier to act on, while B is considerably longer and padded with notary detail.
